**Shipped two fixes to our onboarding agent this week — small root causes, outsized effect.**

Bug 1: ask the agent to open someone's most relevant page, and it'd say "I can't select or open that page." Turned out one of four lookup paths was silently dropping the page ID before it ever reached the "open" step — three others worked fine. Classic drift: one code path updated, three left behind. Fixed all four + added tests that check them in parity, so they can't drift apart again.

Bug 2: on our lighter/faster model, every answer ended with a redundant "...anything else?" — even after the agent already asked a question. Audit found *one* rule created the phrase and *six* existed just to suppress it in edge cases. Deleted the source instead of patching a seventh exception. Score went from 0/3 to 3/3 on that case.

Lesson reinforced: when a prompt rule needs constant patching, the fix is often deletion, not another patch.

---

Revised draft, personal + one example, claims 1 and 6 dropped/fixed:

---

Shipped a fix this week that stuck with me. Someone asked our onboarding agent to open a colleague's most relevant page, and it replied: "I can't select or open that page." I traced it back through four call sites and found the real cause — three of our four page-picker code paths were dropping the page ID before it ever reached the "open" step. Only one had ever been wired correctly; the other three had quietly drifted, unnoticed because they're rarely exercised together.

Fixed all four sites, then added a test that checks all three pickers stay in parity with each other — so next time one drifts, the suite catches it, not a confused user.

Small bug, but it's the kind that erodes trust fast: a tool describing itself as broken instead of just opening the page. Tracing it end to end, all the way to the actual dropped field, beat guessing every time.
